presentingComplaint: Several weeks of constitutional upset with rising creatinine, haemoptysis and new arthralgia
history: 6-week history of malaise, low-grade fever, drenching night sweats and 5 kg unintentional weight loss. Persistent bloody nasal crusting and epistaxis, progressive breathlessness with two episodes of scant haemoptysis, and migratory joint pains affecting wrists, knees and ankles. GP-checked bloods showed a creatinine rise from 90 to 210 µmol/L over 4 weeks with new dipstick haematuria. No preceding sore throat, no travel, no injection drug use. PMH: mild hypertension. No prior renal disease.
examination: Alert, not toxic. Nasal mucosal crusting with early septal collapse. Fine bibasal inspiratory crepitations. Palpable purpuric rash over both shins. Mildly tender wrists and knees without frank effusion. No new cardiac murmur, no neck stiffness. No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly. Fundi normal. Pertinent negatives: no CVA tenderness, no genital or oral ulceration, no digital gangrene.

labs.urinalysis: 3+ blood, 2+ protein, dysmorphic RBCs and red-cell casts on microscopy

imaging: CT chest: bilateral peripheral nodules, two with early cavitation, and patchy ground-glass consistent with alveolar haemorrhage. No consolidation typical of lobar pneumonia.
microbiology: Blood cultures negative; sputum AFB smear negative x2; viral hepatitis and HIV serology negative
differentialDiagnoses: Infective endocarditis with immune complex nephritis
finalDiagnosis: Systemic ANCA-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis) with pulmonary-renal syndrome
citations: ACR/Vasculitis Foundation Management of ANCA-Associated Vasculitis 2021
stewardship: not applicable — non-infective; management is immunosuppression (high-dose glucocorticoids plus rituximab or cyclophosphamide) after excluding active infection, not antibiotics
contraindications: Confirm no active infection/TB before immunosuppression (screen QuantiFERON, hepatitis B/C, HIV)
Dose-adjust cyclophosphamide for renal impairment; PJP prophylaxis co-trimoxazole caution with worsening renal function/hyperkalaemia
edgeCases: MPO/p-ANCA microscopic polyangiitis can present identically without ENT involvement
Drug-induced ANCA vasculitis (hydralazine, propylthiouracil, cocaine/levamisole) mimics GPA
Infective endocarditis can produce low-titre ANCA and RPGN and must be excluded before immunosuppression
expectedMaiK: The triad of upper-airway disease, cavitating pulmonary nodules with alveolar haemorrhage, and a rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (active urinary sediment) with strong PR3-ANCA points to systemic ANCA-associated vasculitis (GPA). This is an organ-threatening emergency: urgently exclude infection/anti-GBM, involve nephrology, and start remission-induction immunosuppression.
expectedNextQuestions: Any haemoptysis volume/desaturation suggesting significant alveolar haemorrhage?
Any drug exposure (hydralazine, PTU, cocaine) that can cause drug-induced ANCA vasculitis?
Any prior sinus/ear disease, saddle-nose or hearing loss?
expectedInvestigations: ANCA panel with anti-PR3/anti-MPO and anti-GBM antibody
Renal biopsy for pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis
Urine microscopy for dysmorphic RBCs/red-cell casts and CT chest
